'''Marcelo Miranda Viana da Silva''' (born 4 March 1962) is a Brazilian [[mathematician]] working in [[dynamical systems theory]].<ref name="abc">{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.org.br/~viana|title=Marcelo Miranda Viana da Silva|website=www.abc.org.br|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171005201144/http://www.abc.org.br/~viana|archive-date=2017-10-05|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="abel">{{cite web|url=http://www.abelprize.no/nyheter/vis.html?tid=46154|title=News: Viana received the first Ramanujan Prize|website=www.abelprize.no|access-date=2014-12-05|archive-date=2017-09-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170928005902/http://www.abelprize.no/nyheter/vis.html?tid=46154|url-status=dead}}</ref> He proved the [[Zorich–Kontsevich conjecture]] together with [[Artur Avila]].

He was a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] in 1993.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/marcelo-viana/|title=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation - Marcelo Viana|website=www.gf.org}}</ref> He received the [[TWAS Prize]] in 1998<ref name="Prizes and Awards">{{Cite web |url=http://twas.org/opportunities/prizes-and-awards |title=Prizes and Awards |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and in 2005 he was awarded the inaugural [[ICTP Ramanujan Prize]] for his research achievements.<ref name="abel" />

Viana was vice-president of the [[International Mathematical Union]] in 2011–2014, and president of the [[Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática|Brazilian Mathematical Society]] (2013–2015).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mathunion.org/organization/ec/ec-1952-2014/|title=International Mathematical Union (IMU): EC 1952-2014|last=the_technician|website=www.mathunion.org|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170515025749/http://www.mathunion.org/organization/ec/ec-1952-2014/|archive-date=2017-05-15}}</ref><ref>[http://www.sbm.org.br/institucional/organização/diretoria Diretoria - SBM - Sociedade Brasileira de Matemática<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

In 1998, he was a [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|plenary speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]], in [[Berlin]].<ref>{{cite web|title=International Mathematical Union (IMU)|website=www.mathunion.org|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Viana}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Viana, Marcelo|chapter=Dynamics: a probabilistic and geometric perspective|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. I|year=1998|pages=557–578|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011737000}}</ref>

Viana is director elected of the [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|IMPA]] (for the period 2016–2019).

Viana is a [[columnist]] for ''[[Folha de S.Paulo]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/colunas/marceloviana/|title=Folha de S.Paulo – Colunistas|work=Folha de S.Paulo|access-date=2017-05-08|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

He was the chair of the executive committee for the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], Rio de Janeiro.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/icm-in-brazil|title=ICM – ICM 2018 in Brazil|website=www.icm2018.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150511043551/http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/icm-in-brazil|archive-date=2015-05-11|url-status=dead|access-date=2017-05-08}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Viana was born in [[Rio de Janeiro]], Brazil, his parents being Portuguese. He grew up in Portugal, and his undergraduate studies were at the [[University of Porto]]. He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree from the IMPA in Rio de Janeiro, with [[Jacob Palis]] as advisor. He is now director at IMPA.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rtp.pt/noticias/pais/portugues-a-trabalhar-no-brasil-recebe-premio-internacional_n22201|title=Português a trabalhar no Brasil recebe prémio internacional|first=RTP, Rádio e Televisão de Portugal - Agência|last=LUSA|date=14 December 2005 }}</ref>

== Work ==

Viana's work concerns [[chaotic dynamical system]]s and [[strange attractor]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.umalca.org/web/?page_id=614|title=UMALCA » Viana|date=4 December 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204204107/http://www.umalca.org/web/?page_id=614|archive-date=4 December 2013}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
Books:
* with José Espinar: ''Differential Equations: A Dynamical Systems Approach to Theory and Practice'' (2021)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/differential-equations-a-dynamical-systems-approach-to-theory-and-practice | title=Differential Equations: A Dynamical Systems Approach to Theory and Practice &#124; Mathematical Association of America (Review by Bill Satzer)}}</ref>
* with Krerley Oliveira: ''Foundations of Ergodic Theory'', [[Cambridge University Press]]
Research papers:
* jointly with [[Artur Avila|AVILA, A.]], "Simplicity of Lyapunov spectra: proof of the Zorich–Kontsevich conjecture". ''[[Acta Mathematica]]''. vol. 198 (2007), no. 1, pp.&nbsp;1–56.
* jointly with [[Jacob Palis|PALIS, J.]], "High dimension diffeomorphisms displaying infinitely many periodic attractors". ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]''. vol. 140 (1994), no. 1, pp.&nbsp;207–250.
* jointly with MORA, L., "Abundance of strange attractors". ''Acta Mathematica''. vol. 171 (1993), no. 1, pp.&nbsp;1–71.
